sounds.ref: Paraphonic chords through the high-pass filter
sounds.blurb: Thin, breathy chords with the bass taken away and a little noise added.
sounds.how: FILTER MODE on HI makes the ladder filter a high-pass: it removes the low part of every note of the chord. A touch of noise adds breath, and the filter contour sweeping downward opens the chord up as it holds.

steps.title: Four triangles and some noise
steps.why:
Soft triangles for the chord notes, with a little pink noise for breath. POLY gives each key you hold one of the four oscillators (the parts that make the raw tone).
- MODE POLY: each new key takes the next oscillator in turn.
- RANGE 8’ on all four: footage comes from organ pipes; 8’ is normal pitch.
- WAVEFORM triangle on all four: soft, with few harmonics.
- FREQUENCY 0 on 2–4: in tune.
- OSC 1–4 on, VOLUME 6 each: even chord notes.

steps.title: High-pass
steps.why:
FILTER MODE HI turns the ladder filter into a high-pass: it removes the low part of every note of the chord instead of the top. The filter contour (Moog’s word for envelope) starts the cutoff high and lets it fall, so the chord fills out as it holds.
- FILTER MODE HI: high-pass, Behringer’s addition to the Minimoog layout. Flip to LO and the chord turns warm and dark.
- CUTOFF −0.5 (about 450 Hz), EMPHASIS 3: where the bass is cut away, with a resonant peak (Moog calls resonance emphasis).
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 3, DECAY 1.5 s: with ATTACK at 1 ms and SUSTAIN 0, the chord starts thin and brings the bass back in over a second and a half.
- Loudness ATTACK 460 ms, SUSTAIN 10: a gentle fade-in, the volume shape a VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) gives on other synths.
- Loudness DECAY 1.0 s, DECAY switch on: a slow fade after release.
- Listen for: chords that start airy and thin and slowly gain body as you hold.

steps.title: Chorus I

The chorus mixes in delayed copies of the sound with the delay swept up and down, which spreads it across the two outputs.
- Chorus ON with CHORUS I: the slow, gentle sweep, for width without wobble.
- Listen for: the airy chords open out to both sides. Switch the chorus off to compare.

sounds.name: Oscillator 4 Wobble Bass
sounds.ref: OSC 4 as a second LFO, brought in with the mod wheel
sounds.blurb: Three oscillators play the bass while Oscillator 4, slowed to LO, wobbles the filter under the mod wheel.
sounds.how: The Minimoog way to get a second LFO: set Oscillator 4 to LO, free it from the keys with OSC 4 CONTROL off, switch it out of the mixer and pick it as the left modulation source. FILTER MODULATION sends it to the cutoff. On the Poly D the mod wheel is the depth, so push the wheel up to hear the wobble. The LFO is still free for vibrato on the other side of MODULATION MIX.

steps.title: Three oscillators for the bass
steps.why:
MONO stacks three oscillators (the parts that make the raw tone) on one note for the bass. Oscillator 4 is kept for the wobble.
- MODE MONO: every switched-on oscillator plays the key you press.
- RANGE 16’ / 16’ / 32’: footage comes from organ pipes; 16’ is an octave below normal pitch, 32’ two octaves, for weight.
- WAVEFORM saw / saw / square: two buzzy saws with a hollow square underneath.
- Osc 2 FREQUENCY +0.1: a hair sharp, so the saws beat.
- OSC 1–3 on; VOLUME 7.5 / 7 / 6: the saws lead.
- Listen for: a thick bass. Oscillator 4 is still on and following the keys for now; the next step changes that.

steps.title: Turn Oscillator 4 into an LFO
steps.why:
The Minimoog way to get a second LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves other controls rather than being heard): slow Oscillator 4 below hearing and free it from the keys.
- RANGE LO: drops Oscillator 4 below audio pitch, so it cycles slowly instead of sounding a note.
- OSC 4 CONTROL off: it ignores the keys, so the wobble speed does not change with the note.
- OSC 4 switch off: taken out of the mixer, so you do not hear it directly.
- WAVEFORM triangle: a smooth up-and-down wobble.
- FREQUENCY 2: now sets the wobble rate. With OSC 4 CONTROL off the knob covers a wide range; here the filter will wobble several times a second.
- Listen for: nothing new yet. It is not routed anywhere.

steps.title: Route it to the filter
steps.why:
MODULATION MIX blends the two modulation sources, picked by the switches under it, and FILTER MODULATION sends the blend to the cutoff. There is no depth knob: the mod wheel sets how much you hear.
- OSC 4 / FILTER EG switch to OSC 4: Oscillator 4 is the left source (FILTER EG would be the filter envelope generator, or contour).
- MODULATION MIX 0: fully left, so only Oscillator 4 is on the modulation bus.
- FILTER MODULATION on: sends it to the cutoff. Nothing moves until the mod wheel is up.
- Listen for: hold a note and push the mod wheel up slowly. The wobble grows from nothing to a deep throb.

steps.title: A resonant, low filter
steps.why:
The filter is a Moog-style low-pass ladder: it keeps the lows and cuts the highs. Setting it low with some emphasis gives the wobble room to move and makes it audible.
- CUTOFF −2 (about 160 Hz): low, so the wobble sweeps upward from a dark base.
- EMPHASIS 5: Moog’s word for resonance, a boost at the cutoff. Makes the moving cutoff sound vocal, “wow-wow”.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 2, DECAY 600 ms: with ATTACK at 1 ms and SUSTAIN 5, a small lift at the start of each note from the contour (Moog’s word for envelope).
- Loudness SUSTAIN 10, DECAY 350 ms: with ATTACK at 1 ms and the DECAY switch on, full level while held, short fade after.
- Listen for: with the mod wheel up, the wobble is much clearer. Change osc 4 FREQUENCY to speed it up or slow it down.

steps.title: Three oscillators on one note
steps.why:
MONO stacks three oscillators (the parts that make the raw tone) on one note: two saws a hair apart that beat slowly, and a square an octave down for body. The base of a warm, singing lead in the style of Daft Punk.
- MODE MONO: in POLY each note would get only one of them.
- RANGE 8’ / 8’ / 16’: footage comes from organ pipes; 8’ is normal pitch, 16’ an octave down.
- WAVEFORM saw / saw / square: bright saws with a hollow square under them.

steps.title: A singing filter
steps.why:
The filter is a Moog-style low-pass ladder: it keeps the lows and cuts the highs. Half open, with emphasis for a vocal edge, and tracking the keyboard so the edge stays with the note as the line climbs.
- FILTER MODE LO: low-pass.
- CUTOFF −0.2 (about 550 Hz): just below the middle. Above 1 it turns brash.
- EMPHASIS 4: Moog’s word for resonance, a boost at the cutoff. The singing edge; above 6 it gets nasal.
- KEYBOARD CONTROL 1 and 2 on: full tracking, so high notes are not dull.
- Listen for: play up the keyboard. The tone stays even and vocal from low to high.

steps.title: Let each note bloom
steps.why:
The filter contour is an envelope (Moog calls envelopes contours) that moves the cutoff each time a note starts. A short attack lets each note open up a moment after it begins, then settle.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 3.5: how much each note opens up.
- ATTACK 1.6 (about 70 ms): the bloom. At 0 every note starts bright instead.
- DECAY 770 ms, SUSTAIN 5: after the bloom it settles halfway, so held notes stay fairly bright.
- Listen for: each note swells slightly brighter just after it starts. Set ATTACK to 0 to compare.

steps.title: Held notes that slide

The loudness contour holds full level, the volume shape a VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) gives on other synths, and glide slides every note into the next.
- Loudness ATTACK 0.3 (2 ms): immediate, no click.
- SUSTAIN 10: full level while held.
- DECAY 600 ms with the DECAY switch on: the fade after you let go.
- GLIDE switch on: the switch beside the keys. Without it the knob does nothing.
- GLIDE knob 3.5 (240 ms): about a quarter of a second per slide. Higher gives a lazier, more swooping line.

steps.title: A square and a triangle, in tune
steps.why:
MONO with a square and a triangle an octave above it, both exactly in tune: a bright but pure tone with no beating at all, in the style of Kraftwerk.
- MODE MONO: both oscillators (the parts that make the raw tone) play each note.
- Osc 1 RANGE 8’, square: footage comes from organ pipes; 8’ is normal pitch. The square gives a hollow, clear body; on sawtooth it would be brassier.
- Osc 2 RANGE 4’, triangle: an octave above, adding brightness without buzz.
- Osc 2 FREQUENCY 0: exactly in tune. Move it off and the two start to beat.
- OSC 1 and 2 on, VOLUME 6 / 4.5: 3 and 4 off. Osc 2 VOLUME sets how much upper octave you hear.

steps.title: Open and even
steps.why:
The filter is a Moog-style low-pass ladder: it keeps the lows and cuts the highs. Here it is fairly open and barely moves, so every note has the same even colour.
- FILTER MODE LO: low-pass.
- CUTOFF 1.2 (about 1.4 kHz): fairly open for a bright tone. Lower it for a softer, flute-like line.
- EMPHASIS 0: Moog’s word for resonance, off, so there is no vocal edge.
- KEYBOARD CONTROL 1 on, 2 off: a third of key tracking, so high notes do not go dull.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 1.5, SUSTAIN 6: with ATTACK at 1 ms and DECAY 350 ms, the contour (Moog’s word for envelope) moves the tone only slightly.
- Listen for: a clean, even tone from start to end of each note.

steps.title: Neat, separate notes
steps.why:
The loudness contour shapes the volume, the job a VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) does on other synths. Each note should sound for as long as the key is held and then stop cleanly, like a machine playing.
- ATTACK 0.3 (2 ms): very short, without a click.
- SUSTAIN 10: full level while held.
- DECAY 250 ms with the DECAY switch on: the short fade after each key, which keeps the notes separate.
- Listen for: neat, even notes with tidy ends.

steps.title: No slides, no effects
steps.why:
The line is meant to be plain, so glide and both effects are switched off.
- GLIDE switch off: notes jump straight to pitch, with no slides.
- Chorus switch off: no stereo sweep; the sound stays in the centre and steady.
- Distortion switch off: no drive, so the tone stays clean.
- Listen for: a simple, exact line. Switch chorus on briefly to hear how much movement it would add.

steps.why:
MONO stacks three oscillators (the parts that make the raw tone) on one note: a saw, a narrow pulse a hair sharp for a reedy buzz, and a square an octave down for weight. A rubbery lead in the style of P-Funk.

- RANGE 8’ / 8’ / 16’: footage comes from organ pipes; 8’ is normal pitch, 16’ an octave down.
- WAVEFORM saw / narrow pulse / square: the narrow pulse adds a thin, nasal buzz on top of the saw.
- Osc 2 FREQUENCY +0.1, osc 3 0: a hair of beating between saw and pulse.
- OSC 1–3 on, VOLUME 7.5 / 6 / 5.5: OSC 4 off. The saw leads, with the pulse and square a little under it.

steps.title: A low, resonant filter
steps.why:
The filter is a Moog-style low-pass ladder: it keeps the lows and cuts the highs. Well down, with high emphasis, it sounds muffled and vocal at rest.
- FILTER MODE LO: low-pass.
- CUTOFF −1.8 (about 180 Hz): kept low so the contour has room to open it. Raise it and the squelch turns into plain brightness.
- EMPHASIS 6.5: Moog’s word for resonance, a boost at the cutoff. The squelch: below 4 notes just brighten; above 8 they whistle.
- KEYBOARD CONTROL 1 on, 2 off: a third of key tracking, so high notes do not go dull.

steps.title: Snap it open on each note
steps.why:
The filter contour is an envelope (Moog calls envelopes contours): each note snaps the cutoff open and lets it fall back. With high emphasis, that is the squelch.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 5.5: how far each note opens.
- ATTACK 0 (1 ms): opens at once.
- DECAY 310 ms: the length of the squelch. Longer gives a slower “wow”.
- SUSTAIN 2: held notes settle back low.
- Listen for: a “yow” on every note. Sweep DECAY while playing to hear it tighten or stretch.

steps.title: Tight loudness

- SUSTAIN 9: held notes keep almost full level.
- DECAY 260 ms with the DECAY switch on: a short fade after you let go.
- Listen for: punchy notes with short tails.

steps.title: Slide between notes

Glide slides every note into the next, so jumps up and down come out as playful whoops. On the Poly D it has an on/off switch beside the keys and a time knob on the main panel.

- GLIDE knob 3 (180 ms): around 3 it whoops; higher, it drags.
- Listen for: the octave drop at the end of the riff swoops down. Switch GLIDE off to hear it jump instead.

- Listen for: an intimate, bowed cello.

steps.title: Vibrato on the wheel
steps.why:
The LFO goes to pitch, as much as the mod wheel says.
- NOISE / LFO LFO: the LFO.
- MODULATION MIX 10: all from the LFO.
- OSCILLATOR MODULATION on: to the pitch.
- LFO RATE 5.2 (3.73 Hz): a slow vibrato.
- Listen for: raise the mod wheel on long notes for a cellist’s vibrato.

context.aenv.attack: In this sound: how slowly each note is bowed.

tweaks.hear: From a firm bow to a slow, sighing one.
From clean notes to sliding ones.

sounds.name: Sitar-Like Buzz
sounds.ref: In the style of Ravi Shankar — sitar
sounds.blurb: A bright, buzzing pluck that bends into its notes, like a sitar.
sounds.how: A sitar’s strings buzz on a wide bridge and bend as they are pulled. Narrow pulses in MONO, a sharp, emphasised pluck that rings and a glide between notes give the buzz and the bends.

steps.title: Buzz
steps.why:
Two narrow pulses.
- MODE MONO: both on each note.
- Osc 1 waveform narrow pulse, Osc 2 waveform narrow pulse: narrow pulses.
- Osc 2 frequency 0.1 (+0.1 st): a hair sharp, for a buzzing beat.
- Osc 3 off, Osc 4 off: only two oscillators.
- Listen for: a bright, buzzing tone.

steps.title: Pluck and bend
steps.why:
A sharp, emphasised pluck that rings, and a glide.
- CUTOFF FREQUENCY 0 (632 Hz): middling.
- EMPHASIS 5: a bright ring.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 3: a pluck.
- Keyboard control 1 on, Keyboard control 2 on: full tracking.
- Filter ATTACK 0 (1 ms), DECAY 3 (350 ms), SUSTAIN 3: a quick pluck that holds a little.
- Loudness ATTACK 0 (1 ms), DECAY 5.5 (880 ms), SUSTAIN 2: instant, then a long ring.
- DECAY switch on: the fade carries on after you let go.
- GLIDE on, GLIDE knob 2 (80 ms): a bend into each note.
- Listen for: a buzzing pluck that bends.

context.filter.emphasis: In this sound: how much the strings buzz.
context.ctl.glide: In this sound: how much each note bends.

tweaks.hear: From a soft pluck to a ringing, buzzing jawari.
From a slight bend to a long, pulled meend.

sounds.name: Celtic Harp
sounds.ref: In the style of Alan Stivell — Renaissance of the Celtic Harp
sounds.blurb: A bright, clear, ringing harp for a gentle folk air.
sounds.how: The Celtic harp is plucked with the fingertips: bright, clear and ringing. POLY triangles and sawtooths, plucked softly with a long ring, let each note of a folk air ring under the next.

steps.title: Clear strings
steps.why:
Triangles and sawtooths, one per note.
- MODE POLY: each note its own oscillator, so they ring together.
- Osc 1 waveform triangle, Osc 3 waveform triangle: triangles; 2 and 4 stay sawtooths.
- Listen for: clear, bright notes.

steps.title: Pluck and ring
steps.why:
A soft pluck and a long ring.
- CUTOFF FREQUENCY -0.3 (514 Hz): soft.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 2.5: a pluck.
- Keyboard control 1 on, Keyboard control 2 on: full tracking.
- Filter ATTACK 0 (1 ms), DECAY 2.5 (260 ms), SUSTAIN 1: quick.
- Loudness ATTACK 0 (1 ms), DECAY 5.5 (880 ms), SUSTAIN 0: instant, then a long ring.
- DECAY switch on: the fade carries on after you let go.
- Listen for: a gentle, ringing harp.

context.aenv.decay: In this sound: how long each string rings.

tweaks.hear: From separate plucks to strings ringing together.
A brighter, wire-strung harp.

sounds.name: Clay Ocarina
sounds.ref: In the style of a clay ocarina
sounds.blurb: A soft, round, hollow flute with a gentle breath, for a simple tune.
sounds.how: An ocarina is a small clay vessel flute: round, hollow and nearly pure. A triangle in MONO, a soft filter, a touch of pink noise and a gentle attack give a round, simple tone.

steps.title: Round
steps.why:
A triangle with a touch of breath.
- MODE MONO: one note at a time.
- Osc 1 waveform triangle: a triangle.
- Osc 2 off, Osc 3 off, Osc 4 off: only one oscillator.
- Noise on, NOISE VOLUME 1: a touch of breath.
- Noise colour PINK: pink.
- Listen for: a round, hollow tone.

steps.title: Gentle
steps.why:
A soft filter and a gentle attack.
- CUTOFF FREQUENCY -0.5 (448 Hz): soft.
- Keyboard control 1 on, Keyboard control 2 on: full tracking.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 0: no movement.
- Loudness ATTACK 1.8 (120 ms), DECAY 2.8 (310 ms), SUSTAIN 10: a gentle start, full, a short fade.
- DECAY switch on: the fade carries on after you let go.
- Listen for: a soft, simple ocarina tune.

context.filter.cutoff: In this sound: how round and soft the ocarina is.

tweaks.hear: From a dark, hooting ocarina to a bright whistle.
From pure to breathy.

sounds.name: Aeolian Harp Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of an Aeolian harp
sounds.blurb: A ghostly, wind-blown drone of shifting harmonics over a fixed tone.
sounds.how: An Aeolian harp is played by the wind, which makes its strings sing shifting harmonics. Oscillator 4, freed from the keys, holds a fixed tone, pink noise is the wind, and a high-emphasis filter swept by a slow contour makes harmonics sing out of it.

steps.title: Wind and a fixed string
steps.why:
Oscillator 4 holds a fixed tone; noise is the wind.
- MODE POLY: the held key takes Oscillator 1.
- Osc 1 waveform triangle: a triangle.
- Osc 2 off, Osc 3 off: off.
- OSC 4 CONTROL off: Oscillator 4 ignores the keys.
- Osc 4 range 16', Osc 4 waveform sawtooth: a sawtooth an octave down.
- Osc 4 frequency 0 (0 st): the fixed string.
- Noise on, NOISE VOLUME 5: the wind.
- Noise colour PINK: pink.
- Listen for: wind over a fixed, low tone.

steps.title: Singing harmonics
steps.why:
High emphasis swept slowly.
- CUTOFF FREQUENCY -2 (159 Hz): low at rest.
- EMPHASIS 7: high, so harmonics sing out.
- AMOUNT OF CONTOUR 4: a sweep.
- Filter ATTACK 6.5 (1.5 s), DECAY 7 (2.2 s), SUSTAIN 3: a slow rise and fall.
- Loudness ATTACK 5 (770 ms), DECAY 7 (2.2 s), SUSTAIN 10: a slow swell, full, a long fade.
- DECAY switch on: the fade carries on after you let go.
- Chorus on, Chorus I on: a slow sweep.
- Listen for: ghostly harmonics singing on the wind.

context.filter.emphasis: In this sound: how strongly the harmonics sing.

tweaks.hear: From a soft breeze to a howling, singing gale.
The fixed string retunes.
